name: apple-safari-mcp
description: Read the text of your open Safari tabs, open or close them, and run JavaScript in one
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to Safari on this Mac.

The valuable tool is tab_get_text: it returns the rendered text of a tab you already have open. No network fetch, no separate login — whatever Safari loaded is what Claude reads.

Know what that means before enabling it. A page behind a login or a paywall is readable, because Safari already rendered it. tabs_list shows every open tab in every window.

Safari must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

run_javascript runs code inside a tab you name, exactly as the page's own script could — no restriction on which tab. Off by default; turn it on below only once you mean for it to work in any tab, signed in or not. It also needs Safari's own “Allow JavaScript from Apple Events” developer setting, off by default on every Mac.

Bookmarks and history need Full Disk Access, granted by hand. Without it those two tools say so rather than returning nothing.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: safari_status
tools.description: Reports whether Safari is running, whether this server may control it, and whether the bookmarks and history files on disk can be read. Opens no page and reads no tab.

tools.name: tabs_list
tools.description: Lists every Safari window and every tab in it, with the page title, the URL and the id needed to read or close that tab. Marks which tab is frontmost in each window.

tools.name: tab_get_text
tools.description: Returns the rendered text of a page that is already open in Safari — what the tab is displaying, not what a fresh request for that URL would return. No network fetch happens, so a page behind a…

tools.name: tab_get_source
tools.description: Returns the raw HTML of a page already open in Safari. SWITCHED OFF in this extension's settings — every call fails until it is turned on.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Opens a URL in a new Safari tab, in the frontmost window, and returns the id of the tab it made. Safari must already be running.

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Closes one open tab. Requires confirm=true and returns the title and URL of what it closed.

tools.name: reading_list_add
tools.description: Saves a URL to Safari's Reading List, optionally with a title and a line of preview text.

tools.name: bookmarks_list
tools.description: Lists saved bookmarks with their title, URL and the folder path each sits in, optionally narrowed to one folder.

tools.name: history_search
tools.description: Finds pages Safari has visited, matching the text against the URL and the page title and bounded by a date range. Newest first.

tools.name: run_javascript
tools.description: Runs JavaScript inside a tab already open in Safari and returns what it evaluated to. SWITCHED OFF in this extension's settings — every call fails until it is turned on below.

allow_javascript.title: Allow running JavaScript
allow_javascript.description: Lets run_javascript execute code inside any tab you point it at — signed in or not, whichever tab is named. Not limited to one site. Also needs Safari's own "Allow JavaScript from Apple Events" developer setting, off by default.
